leading_positions.synthesis: Four of eight members put palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling in their preferred configuration, all with Buchwald and Hartwig as the pair (Linke as one of two parts). Shared: a mature, ligand-controlled general method with demonstrated industrial use, and a two-name configuration. Not shared: how much the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the Migita/Kosugi tin-amide precedent should weigh, and how the citation should be worded to reflect that. Brzezinski and Chabes name B057 only as an alternative; Aili argues in round 1 that its maturity does not by itself outweigh a new design principle.

Two members prefer targeted protein degradation, both with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. Shared: a designable chemical principle (induced proximity to an E3 ligase), independent reproduction and solved ternary structures. Not shared in full: Aili and Chabes both flag that the PROTAC and thalidomide/cereblon molecular-glue strands may be two discoveries that a three-person cap cannot cover (Handa, Ito), and that no PROTAC drug is yet approved. Aqvist lists B004 as an alternative with Handa instead of Ciulli.

One member (the chair) proposes a two-part prize pairing B057 (Buchwald, Hartwig) with B058 base editing credited to Liu alone. No other member prefers B058 in their configuration; Chabes, Sparr and Zou list it only as an alternative, and Aili, Somfai and Brzezinski press the novelty-in-chemistry, timing, CRISPR-2020 overlap and trainee-credit questions. This is a minority position.

One member prefers biomolecular phase separation (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen). Shared with the chair's alternatives: physical-chemical framing and conceptual originality. Not shared: Sparr herself and others raise whether cellular assemblies are true thermodynamic phases in vivo, and Pappu and Mittag fall outside a three-name cap.

One member prefers long-range electron transfer through proteins (Gray, Winkler). Brzezinski himself notes that no other member ranked it first, that Dutton, Moser, Beratan and Onuchic have parallel claims, and that its added distinction beyond the 1992 Marcus prize needs scrutiny; Sparr judges B051 broader.

areas_of_agreement: No single candidate has a majority of five; the largest explicit bloc is four members for B057 (including the chair's two-part configuration).
Every member who commented on B057 describes it as mature, mechanistically understood and widely used, and no member disputes the Buchwald and Hartwig pairing.
Members agree that the cereblon/molecular-glue strand and the PROTAC strand complicate B004 credit, and that no approved PROTAC drug exists yet.
Several members (Aili, Chabes, Linke, Brzezinski) agree that the question of what exactly is being cited must be settled before names are chosen for B004 and B058.
Members agree that unresolved in vivo questions (B051) and ongoing safety data (B058, B004) bear on maturity.
No member reports a conflict with a shortlisted candidate.
scientific_disputes: Whether C-N coupling is conceptually distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize: Zou and Somfai say a different bond type and ligand problem makes it distinct; Aqvist and Zou list the overlap as the main objection, and Sparr is unsure.
Whether degraders, as a new design principle and modality (Aili, Chabes, Aqvist's argument), outweigh the maturity and breadth of a proven method.
Whether base editing is chemistry (new deaminase-based reaction capability) or mainly protein engineering and genome engineering that belongs elsewhere (Somfai, Sparr, Zou, Aili).
Whether condensates are established as thermodynamic phases in vivo, or only in vitro and in selected systems such as P granules and nucleoli (Sparr, Chabes, Aili).
Whether the physical-chemical mechanism of protein electron transfer (B026) adds enough beyond the 1992 prize to compete with broader methods.
attribution_disputes: B057: whether Kosugi and Migita's 1983 tin-amide coupling is a precursor (Aqvist, Somfai, Zou) or a priority claim that should change the citation or add a name (Brzezinski, Zou's reservation).

B004: whether the cap covers the PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, as named by Aili and Chabes) or must include the glue strand (Handa, Ito); Aqvist names Handa instead of Ciulli as the third name.
B058: Liu alone (the chair's configuration; Chabes calls it defensible) versus Liu with Komor and Gaudelli, and the independent Nishida and Kondo cytidine deaminase route.
B051: allocation among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag in three names.
B026: Gray and Winkler versus the parallel claims of Dutton and Moser and of Beratan and Onuchic.
maturity_disputes: B004: no approved PROTAC drug, versus two decades of independent replication and clinical-stage compounds.
B058: about ten years since the first reports, with long-term safety and off-target deamination data still accruing and the 2020 genome-editing prize as a recent predecessor.
B051: about a decade to fifteen years of work with the in vivo phase status contested.
B057 is undisputed on maturity; the disagreement is about novelty relative to 2010.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: No member discloses a conflict with any shortlisted candidate.

Disclosed non-conflicts for transparency: Lund affiliation shared by Linke, Somfai and Sparr; Stockholm University affiliation shared by Brzezinski and Zou; Somfai notes field adjacency to Buchwald and Hartwig; Brzezinski notes scientific closeness to B026; Aili notes scientific proximity to B051.
questions_for_round2: Should the citation for B057 say 'development of the general palladium-catalyzed' coupling, and can the expert record state concretely what the Migita/Kosugi tin-amide work could not do that the ligand-enabled systems did, to settle two names versus three?
Is C-N coupling distinct enough from the 2010 cross-coupling prize that members who treated it as an extension (Aqvist, Sparr) will accept it, and what concrete argument separates the two?

For B004, does the committee honor induced proximity as one principle spanning PROTACs and glues, and if so is the third name Ciulli or Handa, or is there a case for treating them as separate discoveries?
Does the lack of an approved PROTAC drug make B004 premature this year, and does it differ in kind from the clinical-safety maturity concern for B058?
For B058, is a Liu-only citation acceptable, or must Komor, Gaudelli and the Nishida and Kondo route be addressed, and what was new chemically beyond fusing known deaminases to Cas proteins?
Is a two-part prize (for example B057 with B058 or B004) preferred over a single-achievement prize, and does any member besides the chair support a two-part configuration?
For B051 and B026, which claims are settled enough to name a mechanism in the citation, and can either reach majority support given Sparr's and Brzezinski's own reservations?
summary.chair_observation: The explicit preferred positions split across five ballots (B057 four members, B004 two, B051 one, B026 one, plus the chair's B057 and B058 pairing), so no configuration yet reaches five. B057 draws the widest support and is least contested on maturity, with disagreement about novelty and Kosugi attribution; B004 draws substantive support but its attribution and maturity are open; B058 and B051 are held back by timing and evidence questions. Round 2 should settle citation wording and credit boundaries before comparing candidates.
